subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: After repairing proposal-only Crestodian turns, should direct new installs from arbitrary npm, npm-pack, git, local path/archive, and marketplace sources require explicit acknowledgement while ClawHub, bundled, official-catalog, setup, repair, and update flows remain exempt?
rationale: The implementation expresses a coherent source policy, but changing a public noninteractive CLI contract and deciding which executable sources bypass explicit consent require maintainer security and compatibility intent.

options.title: Approve narrowed gate after repair
options.body: Fix proposal preservation, keep acknowledgement limited to direct new arbitrary-source installs, and prove the complete source matrix on the exact merge candidate.

options.title: Keep current install policy
options.body: Decline the mandatory acknowledgement until maintainers choose a different provenance boundary or rollout strategy.

recommendation.title: Approve narrowed gate after repair
recommendation.body: Fix proposal preservation, keep acknowledgement limited to direct new arbitrary-source installs, and prove the complete source matrix on the exact merge candidate.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current provenance implementation and the latest approval-flow revision, making them the best available owner to coordinate repair and policy confirmation.
